_comment: Every number in this file is an ASSUMPTION, not data. prep_population.py reads it and the viewer lists it under Method. Change a value, rerun prep_population.py, reload. Data inputs (LODES, ACS, NHTS, Assessor, OSM) are in the other files of this folder.

officeAttendance.note: Weekday share of office-type jobs (sectors in remoteEligible) whose holder is in the building today: Kastle Back to Work Barometer, Los Angeles weekly average 47.5% for the week to Wednesday 23 September 2026 (unique badge entries relative to the pre-COVID baseline, Kastle's partner buildings), typed by hand. Fixed, no longer a viewer slider (user, 2026-10-08).

otherAttendance.note: Audit 2026-10-09. Weekday presence for in-person jobs: BLS American Time Use Survey 2025, Table 4: 80.5% of the employed worked on an average weekday (sick days, leave, part-time days netted out); Table 5: service occupations 69.2%, used for retail, arts & entertainment, accommodation & food.

weekendWorkShare.note: Audit 2026-10-09. Share of a sector's jobs worked on a typical weekend day. BLS ATUS 2025, Table 5, by occupation (no industry table): service 37.2%, office & administrative support 23.7%; BLS TED 2017: sales 47.5%. Mapped to sectors by hand. default 0.06 = office sectors at the workplace (ATUS weekend work in offices is mostly at home); unsourced.

workHours.note: Audit 2026-10-09. Time at work including lunch, mean and SD (h). Office: BLS ATUS 2025, full-time 8.45 h worked on days worked + about 0.5 h lunch. Shift (outside officeSectors): service occupations 7.44 h, many part-timers, so a wider spread.

lunchOutShare.note: Audit 2026-10-09. Share of present office workers who leave their building for lunch. ezCater 2024 Lunch Report (via Fortune, 2024-10-16): 38% take a lunch break away from their desk every day, an upper bound for leaving the building; no Downtown survey. Lunch times from NHTS work-to-meal trips.

afterWorkOutShare.note: Audit 2026-10-09. ASSUMPTION, no source: share of present workers who stop at an on-site restaurant or bar before going home. FHWA (1995 NPTS) gives about 30% of evening work trips chained to some stop; meals are a minority and only some fall inside the site.

floorHeight.note: Audit 2026-10-09. ASSUMPTION (common values): metres per storey, used to stack people on floors inside the LiDAR volumes. A typical office floor is about 13 ft (4 m); older Historic Core floors are taller. Block job totals are fixed by LODES, so this only moves people between floors and buildings.

jobWeightByUse.note: Audit 2026-10-09. Relative weight per floor area when a block's jobs are split among its buildings: 507 / square feet per worker (EIA CBECS 2018, Table B15: office 507, government 558, health 604, courthouse 690, education 1,314, hotel 3,076, entertainment/culture 2,401, recreation 2,240, mercantile 1,214, food service 480). residential, parking, unknown: assumptions.

sectorUseAffinity.note: Audit 2026-10-09. ASSUMPTION (structure kept): multiplies the weight of a building use for a sector's jobs, so restaurant jobs land in retail space and county jobs in government buildings.

hotelOccupancy.note: Audit 2026-10-09. DTLA Alliance Q1 2026 Market Report (CoStar): 12-month occupancy 68.8% (69.6% a year earlier), about 10% below pre-pandemic.

guestsPerRoom.note: Audit 2026-10-09. ASSUMPTION, no source found: guests per occupied room (plausible 1.3-1.7; Downtown's business and convention mix points to the low end).

ownGarageMinArea.note: Audit 2026-10-09. ASSUMPTION: buildings over this modeled floor area (m2) have their own garage: drivers appear at the building door. No source; pre-1930 Historic Core buildings mostly have none (to refine with year built).

modeByDistance.note: Workers walk or cycle only from homes within this distance (LODES home tract). The overall walk and bike shares, and the drive share by industry, come from CTPP 2017-2021 for the site's tracts (data/ctpp.json), no longer from assumptions.

residentOutings.note: Audit 2026-10-09. Non-work outings (home-based tours) per resident per day, NHTS 2017 rates kept on purpose: the 2022 NHTS (recall-only reporting, ~7,500 households) gives about 0.85 / 0.95 for non-workers / weekends, but under-reports short trips (City Observatory estimate ~20%), and remote work is already in officeAttendance. onSiteShare: ASSUMPTION, no Downtown survey.

hotelGuests.note: Audit 2026-10-09. ASSUMPTION, no public survey found: share of guests out for the day, whose first stop is on site, who dine near the hotel.

visitors.note: Audit 2026-10-09. Daily visitors who are not workers, residents or hotel guests. 'annual' = yearly visitors, spread by visitorWeekendFactor. Grand Central Market 2 million (AP 2017, repeated since); MOCA about 270,000 for both sites (The Art Newspaper 2018 survey; split 60/40 here, the Geffen opens Thu-Sun only), The Broad 846,500 (2024, most-visited US museums list; 896,000 in 2023, The Art Newspaper); Olvera Street / El Pueblo 1-2 million (Wikipedia, Time Out 2017, estimates; 1.5 million used); Grand Park over 1 million (Music Center Form 990 FY2022-23; many come for events); Cathedral over 500,000 (Angelus News). Grand Park and the Cathedral are placed at hand-typed positions (not in the OSM extract). JANM is closed until January 2027. Evening dining: ASSUMPTION (placeholder). 'meals' profile = NHTS start times of trips to buy meals.

visitorArrival.note: Audit 2026-10-09. ASSUMPTION, no visitor mode survey found: how visitors reach the site.

angelsFlightShare.note: Audit 2026-10-09. Share of Grand Central Market visitors who then ride Angels Flight up to Bunker Hill. Derived: Angels Flight carried 1,200-1,500 trips a day when last reported (2010-13); about half go up, most from the Market side: 0.07-0.15 of ~5,500 daily Market visitors. 0.25 would need ~2,750 trips a day.

value.name: Concert at Walt Disney Concert Hall

event.note: Audit 2026-10-09. Walt Disney Concert Hall evening concerts. Seats 2,265 (venue); occupancy 0.85 ASSUMPTION (no LA Phil figure); 8 pm concerts. Audiences park at the garage nearest the hall (60%) or take the Metro (40%, ASSUMPTION).

walkSpeed.note: Audit 2026-10-09. Walking speed, mean and SD (m/s), clipped to 0.6-2.0: Weidmann 1993 review (mean 1.34 m/s, SD 0.26). Slopes are not modelled (FHWA-RD-98-107: no correction below 10% grade).

officeVacancy.note: Downtown LA office vacancy, CBRE DTLA Office Figures Q4 2025 (overall vacancy 34.4%), typed by hand. Job counts come from LODES (jobs that exist), so vacancy does not remove anyone; it is used to check the density of occupied office space per job (a typical office has roughly 15-25 m2 per worker).

residentialOccupancy.note: Occupied share of Downtown LA housing units: about 91%, DTLA Alliance 2025 market report (as summarised by BOMA Greater LA), typed by hand. Residents = housing units (2020 Census, exact) x this x persons per household (ACS B25010, by tract).

groupQuartersMinPop.note: A block with residents but no housing units holds group quarters (dormitories, care homes, shelters) only if the 2020 Census counts at least this many there; smaller counts in such blocks are taken as the Census disclosure-avoidance noise.

eveningShare.note: Share of evenings with a concert at Walt Disney Concert Hall: the LA Phil calendar (laphil.com, viewed 2026-10-09) lists 157 performances at the hall from 9 Oct 2026 to 30 May 2027, 99 of them starting after 5 pm, on 65 weekday and 34 weekend evenings; over a year (261 weekdays, 104 weekend days) 25% and 33%. Events by other presenters are not counted. The typical day carries this expected audience; no toggle.

metroBoardings.note: DATA for calibration, not an assumption: LA Metro FY2026 average weekday boardings, rail only, per station, obtained by a public records request ('FY2026 Metro Ridership by Station', misken67 via Los Angeles Metro Public Records, August 2026, as cited on the stations' Wikipedia pages, viewed 2026-10-09), typed by hand. Station positions from the same pages (Pershing Square: its 4th-5th & Hill entrances). 7th St/Metro Center is a transfer hub: its entrances are assigned but it is not compared. Used only to check the model.

metroLines.note: ASSUMPTION (option B, 2026-10-09): a rail rider takes the line whose branch points toward home. Branch ends are the lines' outer stations (approximate positions, typed by hand from the Metro rail map); each pulls riders by a von Mises weight on the bearing difference, kappa 3 (about +/- 35 deg). Transfers (Union Station, C/K/L lines, Metrolink) are not modelled. Station lines: metroBoardings[*].lines. lineWeight is CALIBRATED, not observed: with equal weights the model gave B/D stations (Pershing Square, Civic Center) 30% of the five compared stations' boardings against Metro's 44% (6,619 of 14,965); B/D odds x (0.793 / 0.433) = 1.83. Because the line shares are fitted to Metro, only the split within each line group remains an independent check. The station weights (stationWeight) are fitted on top of this line weight.

officeSectors.note: Audit 2026-10-09. Sectors on an office schedule (workHours.office, lunch out): information, finance, real estate, professional, management, public administration. Administrative & support (CNS14: janitorial, security, staffing) works shifts.

officeAttendanceWeight.note: Audit 2026-10-09. Share of a sector's jobs that follow office attendance (Kastle); the rest follow otherAttendance. 1.0 for the core office sectors; real estate 0.42 = teleworkable share (Dingel & Neiman 2020, NAICS 53); administrative & support 0.19 and public administration 0.22 = share who actually telework (BLS CPS 2025, Table 60). The government jobs of the Civic Center are mostly in person.

hotelRooms.note: Audit 2026-10-09. Visitor hotels in the site with published room counts (venue listings, Discover Los Angeles, Wikipedia; matched to buildings by address). DTLA Alliance Q1 2026 Market Report (CoStar): 10,751 rooms in all of Downtown, incl. South Park and LA Live outside the site. Hotel Clark (426 S Hill St, 347 rooms) is left out: its reopening was not confirmed. Other Assessor 'hotel & motels' parcels are taken as residential hotels (SROs): no guests.

elevatorWait.note: Audit 2026-10-09. Seconds of waiting per elevator ride (car speed 2.5 m/s, an assumption): NRC Canada Building Digest CBD-190, office waiting interval 25-30 s.

visitorWeekendFactor.note: Audit 2026-10-09. ASSUMPTION: a weekend day brings this many times a weekday's visitors; annual counts are spread over 261 weekdays and 104 weekend days. No source gives day-of-week shares.

theatres.note: Audit 2026-10-09. Evening audiences at the Music Center's other houses, a typical day = annual / 365, same times as the Disney Hall concerts. LA Opera Form 990 FY2018: 38 performances, nearly 108,000 people; Center Theatre Group Form 990 FY2021-22: Ahmanson 200,504 over 157 performances, Mark Taper 60,115 over 148 (a post-COVID year, likely low). Music Center FY2022-23: nearly 800,000 at over 700 ticketed performances.

stationWeight.note: CALIBRATED (user 2026-10-09), not observed: each Metro station's pull on riders of its lines, multiplying the walking-distance choice; fitted by repeated runs so model boardings match metroBoardings (each iteration: weight x (Metro / model)^0.8). Little Tokyo/Arts District is held at 1: most of its riders live outside the site and are not in the model. 7th St/Metro Center (transfer hub) is not compared. With this, the Metro table is a fit, not a check; the LADOT walk counts stay independent.

stationChoiceTemp.note: CALIBRATED with stationWeight (user 2026-10-09): metres of extra walk at which a rider is e times less likely to use an entrance (softmin over walking distance). The first layer used 120 m, so nearly everyone took the nearest entrance and station weights had almost no effect (iteration 1); riders do walk past an entrance to reach a station that suits their trip (line, transfers), so 300 m.

unsheltered.note: People without shelter (user, 2026-10-09: a group of its own). Counts: LAHSA 2025 Greater Los Angeles Homeless Count, street count by census tract (raw volunteer tally of people and of cars, vans, RVs, tents, makeshift shelters; via the Economic Roundtable data library; data/lahsa_tracts.json), times the share of each tract's land inside the site. peoplePerDwelling 1.75 is DERIVED from the USC 2025 methodology report: (43,073 estimated unsheltered adults - 10,411 people counted) / 18,616 dwellings counted, county-wide. Raw tract tallies do not add up to LAHSA's published estimates. People in shelters (LAHSA counts 2,546 in these tracts) are left to the Census group quarters. walksPerDay, walkWindow, walkRadius (m), dwellMin: ASSUMPTIONS, no survey of daily movement.

littleTokyo.note: Little Tokyo visitors, one destination at Japanese Village Plaza (hand-typed position). No published visitor count exists (the Little Tokyo Business Association only estimated an extra 1.5 million in 2024): the annual number is CALIBRATED to the LADOT count on 1st St (Central Ave - San Pedro St) and spread like the other visitors (visitorWeekendFactor). Fitted 2026-10-09 on everyone before thinning.

passersBy.note: People who walk through the site from one edge to another (minCrossM apart): between Union Station, the Arts District, Chinatown, South Park and the rest of Downtown. No source counts them: the daily numbers are CALIBRATED to the LADOT walk counts on the blocks not held out (5th St, Grand Ave and Los Angeles St are kept as a check). Start times follow all NHTS trips of the day. Fitted 2026-10-09 on everyone before thinning (data/raw/population_full.npz).

shops.note: Shops as destinations (user, 2026-10-09). OpenStreetMap maps almost no shops here. Buildings checked by hand in Google Earth / Maps (entities.json, status confirmed) decide first: a checked use naming shops makes a shop (also where the Assessor files the parcel otherwise, e.g. The Bloc), any other checked use (housing, offices, bar ...) rules the parcel out. Elsewhere Assessor parcels with these uses stand in. Weight = shop floor area / sqftPerWeight, capped (ASSUMPTION; a restaurant weighs 1.5): the ground floor (footprint) for mixed buildings, the whole floor area only for wholeBuilding uses. Residents' on-site outings, after-work stops and hotel guests' first stops can go to shops; trips name them 'Shop · ...'.
